slides.head: What high protein dinners will my kids actually eat?
slides.body: Four one-pan dinners with the protein hidden inside food they already like. Swipe for all four.

slides.head: Cheesy egg and black bean quesadillas

items.t: Mash the beans into the eggs
items.s: 1/2 cup black beans and 3 eggs with a pinch of salt. Mashed in, nobody picks them out.
1/2 cup cheddar, 2 minutes a side until golden.

items.t: Cut the kid one into triangles
items.s: Salsa on the side. Spinach and jalapeño go in the grown-up one.
3/4 cup Greek yogurt, 1 tbsp ranch. Save a third for the dip.

items.t: Coat the chicken, press into panko
items.s: 1 lb chicken strips, 1 cup panko, 1/4 cup parmesan, 1 tbsp oil.
15 to 18 minutes, until golden and cooked through.
Tenders with the dip, or sliced over greens with a lemony dressing.

slides.head: Pasta with lentil and turkey sauce

items.s: 1/2 lb ground turkey in olive oil, broken up small.
1/2 cup red lentils, a 24 oz jar of marinara, 1 cup water. 15 minutes, until thick.

items.t: Toss with any pasta they eat
items.s: 12 oz pasta. Chili flakes, parmesan and basil on the grown-up bowl.

slides.head: Stovetop cottage cheese mac and cheese

items.s: 12 oz elbows in salted water. Keep a cup of the pasta water.
1 cup cottage cheese with 1/2 cup milk. This step is the whole trick.

items.t: Stir it in with the cheddar
items.s: 1 1/2 cups sharp cheddar and 1 tbsp butter over low heat, until glossy.
A handful of frozen peas in the last minute, hot sauce on top.

slides.head: All four, with a kid plate and a grown-up plate
slides.body: The full recipes are free on ieatzhealthy.com/recipes. Save this for the next refused dinner.
